traits.build_notes: Liberos are the shortest and lightest players on every level studied (Palao et al. 2014; Marques 2009; Italian, VNL, Slovenian, Serbian and junior studies). STATURE (measured/reported): elite men ~1.85 m (London 2012 liberos 184.8 cm, range 180-190; Okano & Tanigawa 186.7 +/- 8.0 cm; a blog average of ~181 cm); elite women ~1.70 m (USA WNT libero 168.9 cm; Palao reference teams 1.69-1.75 m at 63-66 kg; blog ~169 cm); youth girls ~1.64 m (young female liberos 163.8 +/- 6.2 cm - exact age band of that sample not confirmed, used as the U16 value). REACHES ARE ESTIMATED: standing reach = ~1.32 x stature; spike/block reach are nominal for a libero (she may not attack above the net or block) and were set from standing reach + typical jumps, cross-checked with individual elite-men libero profiles of about 3.10-3.30 m spike / 2.90-3.21 m block and a men sample of unconfirmed (clearly sub-elite) level with liberos of 1.74 m (2.85 / 2.76 m). Exact libero means of Palao et al. could not be retrieved. BUILD: compact, light, low centre of mass, proportionally strong legs (Portuguese junior liberos had the best CMJ), agility and flexibility emphasised (Serbian U17 study); less upper-body mass than middles/opposites. GEAR: jersey of a clearly contrasting colour to the rest of the team (FIVB Official Volleyball Rules, Rule 19 - cited from prior knowledge, not re-verified in this session; no URL), same shorts as the team; knee pads are near-universal for liberos because of constant floor work (sprawls, collapses, pancakes) - common practice, not from a measured source; often long sleeves or elbow sleeves; low-cut indoor court shoes. The libero cannot serve under FIVB rules (some other rule sets allow it), attack above net height, block or rotate to the front row.

traits.build_notes: Middle blockers are the tallest and heaviest players on the team with an ectomorphic build: long legs and very long arms, narrow relative to height, lean (systematic review of the MB; Croatian 13-15 y study: MBs taller and more ectomorphic). Stature: London 2012 Olympic men's MBs 203.8 +/- 4.9 cm (Tsukuba study); top men's MB profiles 2.05-2.09 m (Holt, Piano); women's elite MBs 1.88-1.98 m (Erdem 188, Akinradewo 191, Danesi 195-198); 2017 FIVB U18 girls' MBs 185.9 cm / 71.4 kg; 13-15 y club girls' MBs 174.9 +/- 8.5 cm. U16 value 1.80 m is an estimate between those two youth data sets. Reach: men's MB spike/block 345.6/321.3 cm (Palao et al. 2014 as cited by the MB systematic review, Olympics/World Championships 2000-2012; not checked against the original table); top men's MB profiles 349-357 / 320-338 cm; women: profiles spike 308-315 (Akinradewo 330) / block 300-306 cm, U18 girls' MBs 294.5 / 282.7 cm; women's elite and U16 values are estimates between these, and roster reach values are self-reported and often generous. Palao et al.: spike reach exceeds block reach by about 0.20-0.30 m (men) and 0.15-0.25 m (women); MBs and opposites have the highest block reach. Standing reach is estimated as about 1.32 x stature (no position-specific measured value found). Gear: regular team jersey and shorts/spandex (not the libero colour), knee pads (often low-profile), court shoes; the MB systematic review reports a higher injury risk for MBs, particularly knees and fingers, so taped fingers, patellar straps/knee sleeves and ankle braces are common (gear frequency is an estimate, not measured).

traits.build_notes: ALL NUMBERS ARE ESTIMATES, not values read from a study in this session (full texts could not be opened): typical magnitudes of international opposites on FIVB rosters (self-reported reaches, often generous), standing reach ~1.31 x stature (the app's default), spike reach ~ standing reach + 0.93 m (men) / + 0.68 m (women) / + 0.57 m (U16 girls), block reach ~ standing reach + 0.73 / 0.56 / 0.44 m; U16 values are for selected/competitive club or regional players. Supporting evidence: Palao et al. 2014 (Olympic and World Championship rosters 2000-2012) found height, spike reach and block reach differ by position, with opposites, outside hitters and middles the attackers/blockers; Slovenian female opposites: arm span relates more strongly than height to spike and block reach; Indonesian club men averaged ~3.21 m spike and ~3.11 m block reach (well below international level). Build: among the tallest players on the team (typically a little shorter than the middles, similar to or taller than the outside hitters), long arms (arm span about 1.02-1.05 x stature), powerful and often the heaviest hitter, strong trunk rotators and shoulders because the opposite attacks from front and back row (D/pipe from zone 1) and is the main scorer out of system. Gear: standard team jersey and shorts (not the libero's contrasting jersey), knee pads (often low-profile; some elite men play without), ankle braces common, sometimes a compression sleeve or tape on the hitting shoulder/arm and finger tape for blocking. Handedness: left-handed opposites are common because the set reaches their hitting side first; their attack and approach postures equal a mirrored right-handed outside hitter, while block, defence, cover and transition postures are position-defined and must NOT be mirrored; serves can be mirrored.

traits.build_notes: ALL NUMBERS ESTIMATED: no anthropometric source could be opened in this session because page fetches were blocked and the shared web-search budget ran out. The values are typical figures for international outside hitters (Volleyball World/VNL rosters list height, spike and block reach per player; roster reach values are self-reported and tend to run high) and should be checked before use. Standing reach is taken as ~1.29-1.30 x stature. Spike reach is standing reach + ~0.90 m (men), ~0.65 m (women) or ~0.47 m (U16 girls); block reach is ~0.20 m (men) or ~0.10 m (women and girls) below spike reach. Body build: outside hitters are the all-round passer-attackers, tall but usually a few cm shorter than middle blockers and opposites, with a long-limbed, lean athletic build, strong legs and hips, and a well-developed hitting shoulder and back. Studies support a few qualitative points: upper-body anthropometrics and joint angular velocities matter most for ball speed (Fuchs et al. 2019), men jump higher and use more torso and arm swing than women (Fuchs et al. 2019), and OH/OPP plant with a much deeper knee than middle blockers (Frontiers in Physiology 2026). Gear (visual convention, estimated): knee pads on both knees, usually low-profile sleeve pads worn just below the knee, plus ankle braces or high-top volleyball shoes. Some players wear compression arm sleeves and finger or wrist tape. Women wear fitted shorts and men longer shorts. The outside hitter wears the normal team jersey; only the libero wears a contrasting shirt.

traits.build_notes: ALL TRAIT NUMBERS ARE ESTIMATES (position-specific means could not be read from full texts). Basis: elite men setters profiled 1.98-2.00 m with spike 345-363 cm and block 320-340 cm (Giannelli, Christenson - tall examples); professional men overall spike ~3.43 m / block ~3.27 m (cited from Palao 2014) and setters are generally shorter than hitters/middles, so typical elite setter set slightly lower. Elite women setters profiled 1.78-1.88 m, spike 303-313 cm, block 279-305 cm (Orro, Wolosz, Poulter); elite women overall ~1.82 m with ~2.34 m reach (Valades & Palao). Standing reach estimated as ~1.29-1.30 x stature. U16 girls: competitive (regional/national-pathway) setters estimated ~1.71 m; Serbian U17 national-team mean ~1.77 m (all positions) and setters are shorter than hitters/middles in youth samples; club-level U16 setters will often be 1.62-1.70 m. Build: lean, athletic, usually lighter and shorter than middles/opposites, with lower squat strength and jump than hitters (Marques 2009; national-team data); long arms and strong fingers/wrists matter more than mass. Gear: regular team jersey (not the contrasting libero shirt), shorts (women: spandex), low-profile knee pads, court shoes; ankle braces and finger tape (buddy-taped fingers) are common on setters. Right-handed setter assumed; left-handed setters are mirrored.
